title: Egress capability and route allocation
summary: Nodes may expose outbound capabilities such as jurisdiction, VPN attachment, network class and egress class, but API Client remains authoritative for selecting and reserving the actual outbound session.
invariants: Node identity, capability generation and proofRef must remain available across allocator and API Client seams.
An execution-node placement may establish that a node is capable of satisfying an egress requirement without reserving an egress session.
API Client must re-evaluate the particular egress capability generation when allocating a session.
If no route satisfies every mandatory requirement, the operation fails closed rather than falling back to a weaker route.
Egress capability assertions must use the common trust architecture; nodes do not gain authority by self-asserting labels such as US or CONTROLLED.

provenance.claim: v0.6 binds API route requirements and API-egress capability into placement evidence while retaining hard eligibility.
Allocator explicitly leaves actual API route/session allocation to API Client.
